title: Wikimedia Enterprise Financial Report: Fiscal Year 2025-2026
content:
This is the fifth annual financial report for Wikimedia Enterprise – for the fiscal year (FY) 2025-26.1 This report is published alongside the Wikimedia Foundation’s FY 2025-2026 audit report, as well as key takeaways from the Foundation’s audit report, which outline the full picture of the Foundation’s revenue and expenses. 

The previous reporting period was the first year of profitability for Wikimedia Enterprise; this report shows this has continued, now with net profit of $7.4M – a 92% increase. Revenue has increased 58% and now represents 5.3% of the Wikimedia Foundation’s total. Expenses increased by 28%.

In addition to meaningfully contributing to the financial sustainability of Wikimedia through revenue, Enterprise’s long term contractual relationships have assisted in decreasing the technical and financial burden of scraping on our public infrastructure. This also improves our ability to advocate for improvements in the way Wikimedia content is reused. Within the reporting period there have been many new customer announcements and case-studies published. 

Technical developments of Wikimedia Enterprise during this reporting period are summarized at the end of this report.

title: Highlights from the Wikimedia Foundation and Wikimedia Endowment audit reports for fiscal year 2025-2026
content:
Each year, when the Wikimedia Foundation shares our financial disclosures, we release additional information to explain the numbers more fully. Our goal is to give community members, donors, readers, and other stakeholders insight into how we spend the funds we raise to advance free knowledge.

This post explains key takeaways from the Wikimedia Foundation and the Wikimedia Endowment’s recently-published audit reports (also known as Audited Financial Statements) for fiscal year 2025–2026. These audit reports cover financial activities from July 2025–June 2026, providing a comprehensive picture of the Foundation’s and the Endowment’s financial balances and activities using US accounting standards. Sharing and contextualizing these reports gives us the opportunity to report on how our spending each year aligns with our Annual Plan goals and advances our free knowledge mission.

title: TWU KASU Librarians Wikimedia Outreach Stream 1
content: Through a partnership with Kaduna State University (KASU), the Tyap Wikimedians User Group (TWU) is working to bring Wikimedia projects closer to the university community. The initiative introduces students and lecturers to the knowledge and skills needed to contribute to Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wikimedia Commons, rather than relying on these platforms only as sources of information. It also allows them to document their research, histories, languages, and cultures, making knowledge about their communities more accessible worldwide. TWU and KASU are encouraging members of the university community to take an active role in building and improving the information available online by connecting academic learning with open knowledge. At Kaduna State University, more than 30 participants came together for a two-day training organised by the TWU. Despite power cuts and internet challenges, participants learned how to contribute to Wikipedia, create structured data on Wikidata, and share freely licensed media on Wikimedia Commons.

title: WikiLearn News – November 2026
content:
The latest edition of WikiLearn News is here! Check out the learning opportunities you can enjoy before the end of 2026.

WikiLearn is the free online learning platform crafted by and for the Wikimedia movement. It offers diverse online courses created by Wikimedia affiliates, organizers, and partner institutions that foster social learning and recognize learners’ achievements. The platform is managed by the Community Development team and it’s available in multiple languages.

In June, WikiLearn was upgraded to the more recent Teak version of Open edX. This release allows for a smoother navigation experience for learners and instructors alike, with a highlights being a more modern Studio interface and Markdown support for writing clearer problem components. A set of interactive blocks, including polls, surveys, word clouds, and embedded Google Docs, is easier to find to design courses that invite active participation. We continue to gather input and suggestions that can shape this platform to its best version.

title: An Experience in Kaohsiung as a Conference Participant
content: From May 15–17, 2026, I—a member of the Wikimedia Banjar Community and a volunteer for Wikimedia Indonesia—had the opportunity to attend the 2026 ESEAP Conference in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, representing the Indonesian Wikimedia community, specifically the Wikimedia Banjar Community. This marked the second ESEAP Conference I had attended, following my participation in the 2024 ESEAP Conference in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, Malaysia.

title: Wikimedian Spotlight: Amina Alhassan (Tenacious Ntaawa), Growing Through Persistence and Community Support
content:
The Wikimedia movement grows because people dedicate their time, skills, and knowledge to making information accessible to everyone. Behind every contribution is a person with a story, and through our Wikimedian Spotlight series, we continue to recognize individuals whose efforts strengthen our community.

In this edition, the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group is pleased to spotlight Amina Alhassan, popularly known in the Wikimedia community as Tenacious Ntaawa, for her contributions to Wikimedia projects and her commitment to promoting Ghanaian languages online.

Amina’s Wikimedia journey started during her time at Tamale College of Education. She was introduced to Wikipedia by her senior, Achiri Bitamsimli, who brought the platform to her attention and helped her take her first steps into the Wikimedia movement.

Like many people who are introduced to Wikipedia for the first time, the beginning was not easy. Amina struggled to understand how the platform worked and how to make meaningful contributions. These difficulties sometimes discouraged her, leading her to stop contributing for a while.

title: Three Languages at Bangla WikiConference 2026: Peer Learning and Experience Sharing Among New and Experienced Wikimedians
content: On the first day of Bangla WikiConference 2026 at the BRAC Learning Centre in Rajshahi, new and experienced Wikimedians took part in a special group discussion. Contributors from the Bangla, Syloti Nagri, and Santali languages sat together at one table, using token cards and notes to share their experiences on writing quality Wikipedia articles, peer learning, and promoting open education in their native languages.

title: “Beyond Editing”: a virtual gathering for Africa’s Users with Extended Rights
content:
Most readers never see this work. When a page is vandalised, someone reverts it. When an argument over sources gets heated, someone steps in. When a newcomer makes their first edit, someone checks it and, ideally, says, “Welcome.”

On many African-language wikis, that work rests with a small number of volunteers. They apply community policies, resolve disputes and support contributors, often across several languages and cultures at once, and often without many peers who do the same job.

This week, those volunteers get a space of their own. The African UwERs Virtual Pre-conference runs online on 6 and 7 November, ahead of WikiIndaba 2026. UwERs is shorthand for users with extended rights: administrators, patrollers and other functionaries. The organisers describe it as the first gathering of its kind.

The theme, “Beyond Editing”, is a reminder that writing articles is only one way to contribute. Keeping a wiki healthy, safe, and welcoming is work too. And it needs people.

The pre-conference is built for two groups. If you are a contributor wondering what else you could take on, it sets out to:

  • show you the range of roles and responsibilities available in Wikimedia communities

title: Small wikis in the age of AI: what breaks, what works, and what comes next
content:
On 21 July 2026, the day before Wikimania opened in Paris, I spoke at the Wiki AI pre-conference as an invited speaker. The session was not recorded, so this post is the public record of what was said, the evidence behind it, and what has happened since. For an overview of the whole day, see the organisers’ recap on Diff.

The talk was not about AI in general. It was about what AI does to the smallest wikis, including the ones I work on. I build and maintain tools that small and Indic-language communities rely on, so the question for me is practical: when an editor on a wiki with a handful of active contributors opens an AI assistant, what are they actually getting?

I opened with a question to the room: the same sentence, written in English and in Hindi, which one costs more to process?

The answer is Hindi, by a wide margin. Large language models do not read words; they read tokens. English text packs into few tokens. Devanagari, Bengali and Tamil text breaks into many more. For identical meaning, Hindi can take roughly two to three times as many tokens as English.

title: Digital Ethnography Jember Wins the 2026 Open Education Award for Open Practices
content:
Digital Ethnography Jember (Etno Digital Jember) has received a 2026 Open Education Award for Excellence from Open Education Global (OEGlobal). The winners were announced on September 2, 2026, with the initiative recognized in the Open Practices: How We Share category, which celebrates collaborative practices that expand access to education and open knowledge. From more than 200 nominations representing 49 countries, 16 initiatives were shortlisted as finalists in the Open Practices category. Digital Ethnography Jember was selected as one of four winners for its nomination, Digital Ethnography Jember: Open Cultural Heritage for Education.

Connecting Local Culture with Open Education

Digital Ethnography Jember is a community-based initiative that documents local cultural heritage and shares it through Wikimedia Commons, Wikidata, and Wikibooks. The initiative has produced more than 1,900 openly licensed media files covering traditions, traditional attire, museums, historical sites, local cuisine, and various aspects of Jember’s cultural heritage. These resources can be reused as learning materials, research references, and resources for developing open knowledge.
